title: Points, Lines, Planes, Definitions and Spherical Geometry
seo_title: Geometry Points, Lines, Planes and Definitions Worksheets (TEKS G.4A)
standard_text: G.4A distinguish between undefined terms, definitions, postulates, conjectures, and theorems; G.4D compare geometric relationships between Euclidean and spherical geometries, including parallel lines and the sum of the angles in a triangle
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.4A and G.4D: points, lines and planes, definitions, postulates, theorems and conjectures, and Euclidean versus spherical geometry. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Point, line and plane are undefined; theorems are proved.
key_sub: On a sphere a triangle's angles add to more than 180°.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Undefined terms: point, line and plane. They are described, not defined.
  • A definition uses those terms: a segment is part of a line between two endpoints.
  • A postulate is accepted without proof. A theorem is proved. A conjecture is a guess not yet proved.
  • On a sphere, lines are great circles: there are no parallel lines and a triangle's angles add to more than 180°.

Examples

Example

“Vertical angles are congruent.”

it can be proved

Answer: a theorem

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling a point definedPoint, line and plane are undefined.
Mixing up a postulate and a theoremOnly theorems are proved.
Thinking parallel lines exist on a sphereGreat circles always meet.

items.q: There are 6 points in a plane, and no three of them are collinear. How many lines can you draw through pairs of these points?
items.e: Each pair of points makes one line. The number of pairs is 6 × 5 ÷ 2 = 15. Do not count line AB and line BA twice.

items.q: 5 points are marked on a line. How many segments have two of these points as endpoints?
items.e: Each pair of points is the endpoints of one segment: 5 × 4 ÷ 2 = 10. Short segments and long ones both count.

items.q: There are 7 points in a plane, and no three of them are collinear. How many lines can you draw through pairs of these points?
items.e: Each pair of points makes one line. The number of pairs is 7 × 6 ÷ 2 = 21. Do not count line AB and line BA twice.

items.q: 3 points are marked on a line. How many different rays start at one of these points and go through another one of them?
items.e: Rays that start at the same point and go the same way are the same ray. So each point gives one ray to the right (except the last) and one to the left (except the first): 2 × 2 = 4.

items.q: 10 points are marked on a line. How many different rays start at one of these points and go through another one of them?
items.e: Rays that start at the same point and go the same way are the same ray. So each point gives one ray to the right (except the last) and one to the left (except the first): 2 × 9 = 18.

items.q: There are 3 points in a plane, and no three of them are collinear. How many lines can you draw through pairs of these points?
items.e: Each pair of points makes one line. The number of pairs is 3 × 2 ÷ 2 = 3. Do not count line AB and line BA twice.

items.q: A line and a plane intersect, and the line is not in the plane. What is their intersection?
items.e: A line that pierces a plane meets it in a point.

items.q: 10 points are marked on a line. How many segments have two of these points as endpoints?
items.e: Each pair of points is the endpoints of one segment: 10 × 9 ÷ 2 = 45. Short segments and long ones both count.

items.q: What is the sum of the angles of a triangle in Euclidean geometry?
items.e: In a plane the angles of a triangle add to 180°.

items.q: A triangle on a globe has three 90° angles. What is the angle sum?
Which statement is true in Euclidean geometry but false on a sphere?
c: Two points lie on a line
items.e: On a sphere every two lines meet, so parallel lines never meet is false there.

items.q: On a sphere, how many times do two different great circles intersect?
items.e: Two great circles meet at two opposite points.

items.q: In Euclidean (flat) geometry, how many lines through a point not on a line are parallel to it?
items.e: This is the Parallel Postulate: exactly one.

items.q: What can the sum of the angles of a triangle on a sphere be?
items.e: Spherical triangles bulge outward, so their angles add to more than 180°.

items.q: On a sphere, a “line” is a great circle. How many lines through a point are parallel to a given line?
c: None: every two great circles meet
items.e: Any two great circles cross, so on a sphere there are no parallel lines.

items.q: Which is a “line” in spherical geometry?
c: A line of latitude near the North Pole
A straight tunnel through the Earth
items.e: A line on a sphere is a great circle, like the equator.

items.q: Which plane is parallel to plane ABCD?
items.e: Opposite faces of a box never meet: plane EFGH. The other faces share an edge with plane ABCD.

items.q: Which best describes this pair? The edge where a wall meets the floor, and the edge where that wall meets the next wall.
items.e: They meet at a corner at a right angle: perpendicular lines.

items.q: Which edge intersects FG and is perpendicular to it?
items.e: The edges that share an endpoint with FG meet it at a right angle in a box: GH.

items.q: Which best describes this pair? A hallway's floor and ceiling.
items.e: The floor and ceiling never meet, like the top and bottom of a box: parallel planes.

items.q: Which edge is skew to DH?
items.e: Skew lines never meet and are not parallel, so no flat surface holds both. BC is skew to DH.

items.q: Plane ABCD and plane BCGF intersect. What is their intersection?
items.e: Two planes meet in a line. The points in both planes are B and C, so they meet in line BC.

items.q: Which best describes this pair? A road on a bridge and a road below it that goes in a different direction.
items.e: They never meet and do not go the same way, and they are at different heights: skew lines.

items.q: Which edge is skew to BC?
items.e: Skew lines never meet and are not parallel, so no flat surface holds both. DH is skew to BC.

items.q: Which edge is skew to EF?
items.e: Skew lines never meet and are not parallel, so no flat surface holds both. DA is skew to EF.

items.q: Which edge intersects BF and is perpendicular to it?
items.e: The edges that share an endpoint with BF meet it at a right angle in a box: AB.

items.q: Which edge is parallel to BF?
items.e: Parallel edges point the same way and never meet. BF and CG are in the same face and never meet: CG.

items.q: Which plane is parallel to plane ADHE?
items.e: Opposite faces of a box never meet: plane BCGF. The other faces share an edge with plane ADHE.
